objectClass.primaryType: medieval cooper's bench with open horizontal barrel, stave rack, cask and hoop-heating tools
objectClass.notes: The open barrel interior, individual stave ends and separate hoop layers define the trade; a closed generic barrel on a table is a hard failure.

reasoning: The partly assembled barrel depends on a radial array of tapered curved staves and a visible hollow interior.
Cradle, rope clamp, fitted hoops, loose hoops, tools, brazier and spare-stave rack form multiple overlapping but distinct workflow systems.
Fresh-cut wood, aged bench wood, iron, rope, soot and pale shavings require independent surfaces.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Complex depth is required by the radial barrel shell, tool set, stave rack, hoop system and action-ready clamp/cradle hierarchy.

unknownsToResolveBeforeImplementation: The barrel's hidden rear stave joints are inferred by radial continuation.
Loose floor tools are retained only where they strengthen recognition without destroying sparse placement.

details.description: The horizontal unfinished barrel has a deep visible cavity and a jagged ring of individually projecting stave ends.
Twenty curved tapered oak staves form a bulged radial shell with visible seams and fresh-cut front grain.
Four dark forged hoops wrap the barrel at distinct axial positions and sit proud of the oak shell.
A thick rope clamp crosses the barrel and winds around a projected windlass with a visible knot and tail.
Two notched cradle blocks and raised end stops fully contact and support the horizontal barrel.
A thick shaving bench uses broad beams, splayed legs, pegs, a drawer and strongly worn chamfered edges.
A braced rack holds twelve spare staves at varied height, width, color and lean angle.
The finished side cask uses its own sixteen-stave body, three hoops, lid, bung, tap and support feet.
A banded iron brazier on four feet contains black charcoal and restrained orange ember cores.
A curved dark drawknife with two wooden handles lies fully dimensional across the foreground.
A croze plane, hoop driver and two distinct mallets use separate bodies, blades and handle profiles.
A spiral auger and U-shaped brace expose twisted metal shafts and separate turned wooden grips.
Three independent forged hoops overlap on the ground with visible band thickness and edge highlights.
Pale curled shavings scatter in controlled clusters under the bench and around the planes.
Fresh pale staves and end grain contrast with dark aged bench wood, soot-darkened brazier contact and polished tool handles.

anatomy.note: Object domain; character anatomy is not applicable.

definitionOfDone: The open radial stave shell, separate hoops, attached cradle and clamp, stave stock, completed cask, heating brazier and dimensional cooper tools remain recognizable from main and side views.

qualityCriteria: Hollow interior, projecting stave ends, radial seams, bulge and four separate hoops are all visible.
Heavy bench, notched cradle and rope windlass visibly support the barrel.
Spare stave rack and completed tapped cask use distinct construction and scale.
Brazier, drawknife, planes, mallets, auger, brace, loose hoops and shavings remain dimensional and readable.
Fresh oak, aged oak, end grain, iron, rope, soot, embers and shavings respond independently.

antiShallowSpecRules: A closed generic barrel may not replace the unfinished open shell.
The barrel may not be a cylinder with painted seam lines.
Tools may not be flat plates or hidden under the bench.
Loose hoops and shavings must not dominate the footprint.

authoringInstruction: Assessment completed from the admitted reference before implementation.
